arxiv-2205-15367.title: Non-Markovian Reward Modelling from Trajectory Labels via Interpretable Multiple Instance Learning
arxiv-2205-15367.creator: Joseph Early Tom Bewley Christine Evers Sarvapali Ramchurn
arxiv-2205-15367.description: Abstract We generalise the problem of reward modelling (RM) for reinforcement learning (RL) to handle non-Markovian rewards. Existing work assumes that human evaluators observe each step in a trajectory independently when providing feedback on agent behaviour. In this work, we remove this assumption, extending RM to capture temporal dependencies in human assessment of trajectories.

arxiv-2404-05800.creator: J. Cepila, J. G. Contreras, M. Vaculciak
arxiv-2404-05800.description: Abstract In this proceedings a solution of the target-rapidity Balitsky-Kovchegov (BK) equation is presented considering the complete impact-parameter dependence, including the orientation of the dipole with respect to the impact-parameter vector. The target-rapidity formulation of the BK equation introduces non-locality in rapidity. Three different prescriptions are considered to take into account the rapidities preceding the initial condition.

arxiv-2411-09644.title: Neural Operators Can Play Dynamic Stackelberg Games
arxiv-2411-09644.creator: Guillermo A. Alvarez guialv@umich.edu, Ibrahim Ekren iekren@umich.edu, Anastasis Kratsios kratsioa@mcmaster.ca, Xuwei Yang yangx212@mcmaster.ca
arxiv-2411-09644.description: Abstract Dynamic Stackelberg games are a broad class of two-player games in which the leader acts first, and the follower chooses a response strategy to the leader’s strategy. Unfortunately, only stylized Stackelberg games are explicitly solvable since the follower’s best-response operator (as a function of the control of the leader) is typically analytically intractable.

arxiv-2506-11657.title: Fast parallel transient electromagnetic modeling using a uniform-in-time approximation to the exponential
arxiv-2506-11657.creator: Ralph-Uwe Börner, Stefan Güttel
arxiv-2506-11657.description: Abstract A new approach for the parallel forward modeling of transient electromagnetic (TEM) fields is presented. It is based on a family of uniform-in-time rational approximants to the matrix exponential that share a common denominator independent of the evaluation time points. The partial fraction decomposition of this family is exploited to devise a fast solver with high parallel efficiency.

pmc-10605842.description: The transition from notochord to vertebral column is a crucial milestone in chordate evolution and in prenatal development of all vertebrates. As ossification of the vertebral bodies proceeds, involutions of residual notochord cells into the intervertebral discs form the nuclei pulposi, shock-absorbing structures that confer flexibility to the spine.

pmc-11452621.title: NPC1 links cholesterol trafficking to microglial morphology via the gastrosome
pmc-11452621.creator: Joanna Zareba, Elena F Cattaneo, Ambra Villani, Alaa Othman, Sebastian Streb, Francesca Peri
pmc-11452621.description: Microglia play important roles in brain development and homeostasis by removing dying neurons through efferocytosis. Morphological changes in microglia are hallmarks of many neurodegenerative conditions, such as Niemann-Pick disease type C. Here, NPC1 loss causes microglia to shift from a branched to an ameboid form, though the cellular basis and functional impact of this change remain unclear.

pmc-11641450.title: Therapeutic Potential of Natural Compounds to Modulate WNT/β-Catenin Signaling in Cancer: Current State of Art and Challenges
pmc-11641450.creator: Anna Gajos-Michniewicz, Malgorzata Czyz
pmc-11641450.description: Targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved the clinical outcome of cancer patients; however, the efficacy of treatment remains frequently limited due to low predictability of response and development of drug resistance. Therefore, novel therapeutic strategies for various cancer types are needed. Current research emphasizes the potential therapeutic value of targeting WNT/β-catenin dependent signaling that is deregulated in various cancer types.

pmc-12435647.title: Clinical, virological, and antibody profiles of overlapping dengue and chikungunya virus infections in children from southern Colombia
pmc-12435647.creator: Daniela Polanía-Espinosa, Sebastián Castro-Trujillo, Carlos F. Narváez
pmc-12435647.description: BackgroundDengue and chikungunya are arboviral diseases with overlapping clinical characteristics. Dengue virus (DENV) is endemic in Colombia, and in 2014/2015, the chikungunya virus (CHIKV) caused an epidemic that resulted in over 350,000 cases. Since then, both viruses have been actively co-circulating. The early and accurate identification of pediatric infection caused by DENV or CHIKV is essential for proper medical management.

pmc-12547520.title: DRP-PSM: Multi-Level Feature Integration Reveals Hierarchical Contributions to Pathogenic Synonymous Mutation Prediction
pmc-12547520.creator: Jinsong Cai, Fangfang Jin, Na Cheng, Junfeng Xia, Chen Ye
pmc-12547520.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Synonymous mutations, a unique class of genetic variants, do not change the amino acid sequence of the encoded protein. Despite this, they can impact protein stability and function through diverse molecular mechanisms. Such subtle alterations can contribute to disease initiation and progression, making the prediction of pathogenic synonymous mutations crucial for understanding disease mechanisms as well as improving clinical diagnosis and treatment.

pmc-13147103.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1898 A DECADE OF STROKE EPIDEMIOLOGY: INCIDENCE, MORTALITY, AND DISABILITY TRENDS FROM THE GLOBAL BURDEN OF DISEASE STUDY, 2013-2023
pmc-13147103.creator: Gita Diah Prasasti, Afifah Az Zahra
pmc-13147103.description: Background and aimsStroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term neurological disability worldwide. Despite advances in acute stroke care in several regions, the global burden of stroke remains substantial and heterogeneous. Contemporary epidemiological evidence is required to determine whether improvements in stroke management have translated into reductions in population-level incidence, mortality, and disability.

pmc-13240446.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Salivary Periodontal Biomarkers Is Reduced in Patients With Crohn's Disease
pmc-13240446.creator: Alisa Toivanen, Nur, Ismo Räisänen, Mervi Gürsoy, Ulvi Kahraman Gürsoy, Timo Sorsa, Jaana Rautava
pmc-13240446.description: ObjectivesPatients with Crohn's disease (CD) are at increased risk of developing periodontal disease and may benefit from salivary biomarker–based monitoring for early detection and management. Given the previously reported reduced specificity of the salivary aMMP‐8 test in CD, this study aimed to evaluate alternative salivary biomarkers for periodontal disease.
